walkthroughs.title: Get Started with LiquidJava
walkthroughs.description: Set up your project and discover verification, views, commands, and logs.

steps.title: Set up Java support
steps.description:
Install Java and **Language Support for Java by Red Hat**, then open your Java project folder.
[Get Java language support](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=redhat.java)

steps.title: Add the annotation API
steps.description: Add `liquidjava-api` to your Maven or Gradle project to use annotations such as `@Refinement`.

steps.title: Verification and status
steps.description: Open or save a Java file to verify it. Watch the **LiquidJava** indicator in the bottom status bar.

steps.title: Find LiquidJava commands
steps.description:
Open the **Command Palette**, type `LiquidJava`, and choose a command.
[Open Command Palette](command:workbench.action.showCommands)

steps.title: Understand diagnostics
steps.description:
The **Verification** tab compares **Found** with **Expected**. Click a location to jump to the error.
[Open LiquidJava view](command:liquidjava.showView)

steps.title: Inspect context
steps.description:
The **Context** tab shows variable refinements, aliases, and ghosts at your cursor or selection.
[Open LiquidJava view](command:liquidjava.showView)

steps.title: Explore state machines
steps.description:
The **State Machine** tab shows object states and method transitions declared with `@StateSet` and `@StateRefinement`.
[Open LiquidJava view](command:liquidjava.showView)

steps.title: Check the logs
steps.description:
The **LiquidJava** output channel records extension and verifier activity. Use it to investigate startup or verification problems.
[Show LiquidJava logs](command:liquidjava.showLogs)

steps.title: Learn LiquidJava interactively
steps.description:
Try refinements, method contracts, object states, and ghosts in the browser. No local setup needed.
[Open interactive tutorial](https://liquid-java.github.io/liquidjava-interactive-tutorial/)
